secs.t: Reading Comprehension: A Day at the Beach
secs.p:
Last Saturday, a group of students visited a beach with their teachers. They were excited because they were going to learn about marine life and how to protect the environment. Before they started, their teacher explained that rubbish can be dangerous for sea animals.
At first, Sami felt nervous because he had never taken part in a beach clean-up before. His friend Lina was calm and encouraged him to join her. Together, they collected plastic bottles, bags and other rubbish from the sand. Lina was very generous and shared her gloves with another student who had forgotten to bring a pair.
After an hour, Sami began to feel tired and developed a headache. His teacher asked him to sit in the shade and drink some water. After a short rest, he felt better and decided to continue helping his friends.
During the clean-up, the students also noticed some birds searching for food near the rubbish. Their teacher explained that plastic and other waste can harm animals if they eat it or become trapped in it. The students became more careful as they worked and made sure they collected even the smallest pieces of rubbish.
By the end of the morning, the beach looked much cleaner. The students were proud of their work. They realised that small actions can make a big difference to the environment and that everyone has a responsibility to protect marine life.

q.text: Why did the students visit the beach?
opts: To learn about protecting the environment.
To play games on the sand.
To go swimming with their teachers.

q.text: Why was Sami nervous at first?
opts: He was afraid of the sea.
He had never joined a beach clean-up before.
He did not want to work with his friends.

q.text: What does the word “generous” mean in the passage?
opts: Willing to share and help others.

q.text: What did the students collect from the beach?
opts: Plastic bottles, bags and other rubbish.

q.text: What happened to Sami after an hour?
opts: He went swimming in the sea.
He became angry with his friends.

q.text: What can we infer about the students at the end of the visit?
opts: They understood that protecting the environment is important.
They thought cleaning the beach was a waste of time.
They decided that only teachers should protect marine life.

q.text: What did the students do to help protect the environment?
opts: They collected rubbish from the beach.
They played games on the sand.

secs.t: Reading Comprehension: A Day at the Farm
secs.p:
On Thursday, Year 5 went on a trip to a farm near Al Ain. The children were cheerful on the bus because they were going to learn where food comes from. The farmer welcomed them and showed them how to look after the animals.
Huda felt nervous at first because she had never touched a goat before. Her friend Omar was outgoing and talked to the farmer happily. He told Huda that the goats were gentle. Soon, Huda was feeding them and smiling.
Then the students collected eggs and picked fresh tomatoes. Omar was generous and gave some of his tomatoes to a boy who had not found any. After lunch, Omar ate too much and got a stomach ache. The teacher asked him to sit down and rest. He felt better after twenty minutes.
Before they left, the farmer explained that farms need water and care. The students promised to save water at home. They understood that everyone can help to protect nature.

q.text: Why did Year 5 go to the farm?
opts: To learn where food comes from.

q.text: Why was Huda nervous at first?
opts: She was afraid of the farmer.
She had never touched a goat before.

q.text: What does the word “outgoing” mean in the passage?
opts: Friendly and happy to talk to people.

q.text: What did the students collect and pick?
What happened to Omar after lunch?
opts: He fell asleep on the bus.

q.text: What can we infer about the students at the end of the trip?
opts: They learned that saving water is important.

q.text: How did Omar show that he was generous?
opts: He ate all the tomatoes himself.
He took eggs from the farmer.
He gave some of his tomatoes to a boy who had not found any.
